So that the sweet Jesus—who in these times is lamentably driven out of the hearts of many men, because each seeks what is his own and not what belongs to Jesus Christ—might ignite his love within them, impress his honey-flowing Name upon them, and preserve it within them.

In addition to this, the disciples of Eternal Wisdom must visit their Lady and Spouse with special honor and devotion on certain days of the year.

**The first day** is the first Sunday in the month of August, on which the Books of Wisdom are begun [to be read] in the Church of God.

**The second day** is the eighth day before the feast of Christ <note>Christmas</note>, when the Antiphon is sung: *O Sapientia* <note>original: "O Sapientia," meaning "O Wisdom." This is one of the "O Antiphons" sung in the days leading up to Christmas.</note>. From this day until the Night in which Eternal Wisdom deigned to enter this world in bodily form, they shall offer to Eternal Wisdom a special remembrance, Antiphon, Collect, or other prayer, according to each person's devotion. But if he is a priest, and reads the Mass of Eternal Wisdom with devotion, he will perform a deed most pleasing to her.

**The third day** is the Circumcision of the Lord <note>January 1st, New Year's Day</note>. On this day the new year begins; and according to the custom of some lands, one friend is used to sending a gift to another and wishing them a blessed New Year. Likewise, a disciple of Wisdom, to incite Divine Love, shall go to his heavenly Spouse and entreat from her a new and blessed year for himself, all his fellow students, and the entire Church.

**The fourth day** is the Sunday in

<column-break/>

Shrovetide <note>Fasznacht; the period of Carnival before Lent</note>, which the foolish lovers of the world hold as a festival, on which they come together and defile it with many wicked deeds and vain comforts. In order that a servant of Wisdom may clearly show <note>erzeige</note> that Wisdom is his only joy and rest <note>ruh</note> both in this life and the life to come <note>Leben</note>, he shall do what is written <note>geschrieben</note> below.

**The fifth day** is the first day of May <note>May/Mai</note>, when the most delightful springtime shows <note>erzeigt</note> itself as pleasant to all people in all the earth's plants <unclear>growth</unclear>. In this night, in some places, it is the custom for young men to place green trees before the doors of their lovers as a sign of their love. Now, so that out of a worldly deed a good devotion may be made <note>gemacht</note>, and what worldly lovers do to please a <note>einem</note> mortal human, the children of Wisdom shall perform in a spiritual <note>geistlicher</note> manner for the Creator of all things. They shall do this all the more diligently because the Divine <note>Göttliche</note> Friend far surpasses all humans; they shall offer to her on this day either a rose <note>Rosen</note> or a special prayer <note>auffopffern</note>.

On each of the five mentioned <note>gemelten</note> days, the disciples of Eternal Wisdom <note>Weißheit</note> shall keep [the day] with special devotion and <note>vnnd</note> shall say one hundred Our Fathers, with as many Hail Marys, or something else <note>anders</note>, or hear Mass; or (if they are priests) read Mass, or offer a candle, or <note>oder</note> perform another good work to the praise and honor of <note>der</note> Eternal Wisdom, which is the <note>das</note> eternal light. This serves as a certain sign that faithful disciples in this transitory <note>vergänglichen</note> time recognize all their salvation to come from the Spouse <note>Gesponß</note> alone, and that they wish to desire and hope for everything from her alone, and that <note>daß</note> her love alone shall shine <note>leuchten</note> and burn in their hearts; and if perhaps the...

But now, O sweetest Heart of Jesus Christ, I rise early in the morning to you and greet you out of the inner affection of my heart. Let a thousand times a thousand from the heavenly host who serve you greet you on my behalf, and let ten

<column-break/>

> thousand times a hundred thousand times thousand who stand before you praise you. Let all creatures praise you on my behalf, and bless your glorious Name—the shield of our protection—into eternity. Amen.

In addition to this, the disciples of Eternal Wisdom shall honor the Mother of Eternal Wisdom with the highest affection, as she is ready to receive them as children entrusted to her Son, and to take maternal care of them. Therefore, every apprentice shall daily say the Angelic Salutation <note>original: "Englischen Gruß," referring to the Hail Mary (Ave Maria)</note> nine times in her honor. Once in the morning when he rises, bending his knees, he shall offer all the works he intends to perform throughout the day to the Queen of Heaven, so that she, as the venerable and most beloved Mother, may present them to her Son, the highest King. Through the intercession of such a great Mediatrix <term>Mittlerin: a female mediator, specifically Mary in her role as an intercessor between humanity and God</term>, these works—which might otherwise be small, insignificant, and unpleasing if they were brought to God the Lord by a sinful person without this Mediatrix—may be made acceptable. And so that he may sleep more securely, he shall do the same when he wishes to go to rest, and desire that whatever was neglected during that day be restored through her, whatever was done poorly be improved through her, and through her be made pleasing to God the Lord.

The remaining seven Hail Marys he shall say to the sweetest heart of the Mother of God, as the most affectionate refuge of all sinners, so that she, as the most pleasant dwelling of Eternal Wisdom, may open the treasury of all the Lord’s mercy, and direct such mercy upon all apprentices of Eternal Wisdom at their [end]...

[...to their] final end / that she <note>Eternal Wisdom is personified as female in Suso's work, following the Latin *Sapientia* and Greek *Sophia*.</note> may then graciously protect them / and accompany them as an inseparable companion to the Heavenly Palace. 

But if some are so weak / or burdened with permissible business / that they cannot occasionally attend to the aforementioned things at a certain time / or if, out of the hardness of their heart (as mentioned), they cannot perform everything / they should daily say nine **Our Fathers** <note>original: "Vatter vnser"</note> / and nine **Hail Marys** <note>original: "Ave Maria"</note> / and make their intention inwardly / or silently / just as others do explicitly / Then it is already enough.

The salvation of the world flows forth from you.
A beginning you are of goodness,
A hope of all joy.
You are a dear fountain of grace,
My heart’s guest / its joy / and home.

V. Convert us, O God our Savior.
R. And turn your anger from us.
V. O God, attend to my help.
R. Lord, make haste to help me.
Glory be to the Father / <term>etc.</term>
**Antiphon.** In the heights.
**Psalm.** <note>Psalm 13:3-6.</note> Enlighten my eyes / so that I do not sleep in death. So that my enemy might not boast / that he has become powerful over me. Those who plague me / will be glad / if I am driven away. But I hope in your mercy / my heart rejoices in your salvation / I will sing to the Lord / because he has done good to me / and to the Name

Wisdom teaches sobriety / justice / and virtue / than which nothing is more useful in the life of man.
Thanks be to God.
I will sleep and rest with him in peace. I will not let my eyes sleep / nor let my eyelids fall in sleep. I will sleep and rest. <note>original: "Ich will im frieden mit ihm schlaffen..." These verses combine elements of Psalm 4:8 and Psalm 132:4, emphasizing rest in God's care.</note>

<header>Hours of Eternal Wisdom.</header>

### Hymn.

Jesus reigns in peace,
He surpasses all sense and mind.
My heart longs for this peace,
Ah, that I might soon be granted this.
The host of holy angels praises you,
They sing your praise forevermore.
Jesus refreshes the whole world,
Which he sets at peace with God.
Jesus has ascended to the Father,
He reigns over all the hosts of angels.
My heart has departed from me,
And runs after him until it catches him.

->Eternal Wisdom.<-
℣. Her seat is in peace. <note>In traditional Christian mysticism, "Wisdom" (Sophia) is often personified and associated with the peace of the divine presence.</note>
℟. And her dwelling in Zion.

### Canticle.
<note>This is the "Nunc Dimittis" or the Song of Simeon from the Gospel of Luke. It is the traditional song for Compline, the final prayer before sleep, symbolizing both the end of the day and the end of life.</note>

O Lord, now let your servant depart in peace according to your word, <term>etc.</term>

**Antiphon.** O glorious King, you who are always praiseworthy among your saints, and yet are inexpressible; Lord, you dwell in us, and your holy Name

<column-break/>

is called upon over us; do not forsake us, our God; rather, deign, O blessed King, to place us among your saints and chosen ones on the Last Day. <note>The "Last Day" refers to the Day of Judgment or the end of the world in Christian theology.</note>
℣. Lord, hear my prayer.
℟. And [let] my cry [come to you], <term>etc.</term>

### Prayer.

Lord, we pray you, look graciously upon our weakness, and pour into us the taste of eternal Wisdom, so that after tasting her honey-flowing sweetness, we may despise all earthly things and may always cling to you, the highest good, with burning desire. Through the same our Lord Jesus Christ your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the most Holy Spirit, true God from eternity to eternity. Amen.
℣. Lord, hear my prayer.
℟. And let my cry come to you.
℣. Let us praise the Lord,
℟. And give thanks to God.

# JUDGMENT OF THE APOSTOLIC 
# INQUISITOR.

Since I have learned—from the faithful and sincere report of a certain Reverend Father and Theologian of the Order of Preachers <note>original: "Ordinis Praed."; the Dominicans</note> and Preacher, to whom this task was entrusted—that this translation of the works of the most enlightened man, Blessed Henry Suso of the Order of Preachers, made from the Latin version of Surius <note>Laurentius Surius (1522–1578) was a Carthusian monk who translated many mystical works into Latin to make them accessible to an international scholarly audience.</note> into the High German language <note>original: "idioma Superioristicum Germanicum"</note>, is genuine, well-arranged, and entirely consistent with the original; and from which great fruit in the pious minds of Christ’s faithful and a most abundant progress in the exercises of devotion can certainly be hoped for, I judge it to be most useful that it be printed, for the sake of the German nation and as an ornament to Cologne of the Ubii <note>Cologne was often referred to by its Roman name, "Colonia Agrippina" or "Colonia Ubiorum," after the Ubii tribe.</note>, where the author once lived most holily in the monastery <note>original: "Asceterio," a term for a place of ascetic practice or a monastery.</note> of the Dominican Fathers and shone forth wonderfully through his examples of virtue. Cologne, the year 1661, the 28th of January.

->Friar Nicolaus Haustadt, of the Order of Preachers, Doctor of Sacred Theology,<-
->and Senior Ordinary Professor, Apostolic General Inquisitor,<-
->signed with his own hand.<-

---

### CENSORSHIP OF THE ORDINARY.

The works of Blessed Henry Suso of the Order of Preachers, faithfully translated from the Latin version into the German language by the Reverend Father Anselm Hoffman of the Order of Friars Minor Recollect, and highly praised by learned men as being thoroughly useful to the faithful people and not contrary to faith or good morals, we permit to be published in print. Cologne, the 29th of January, 1661.

->Adrianus de Walenburch, Priest-Canon of the Metropolitan Church of Cologne,<-
->and Ordinary Censor of Books.<-

<meta>This page continues the formal ecclesiastical approvals for the publication of Blessed Henry Suso's works. While the previous page focused on a translation into High German, the current page provides the "Judicium" (Judgment) and "Censura" (Censorship) for a version associated with French and Latin sources, reflecting the complex linguistic history of Suso's mystical writings in the 17th century.</meta>

# JUDGMENT OF THE APOSTOLIC 
## INQUISITOR

Having received a report of the records and letters from the Reverend Father Friar Nicolaus of Harburg, an Ecclesiastical Preacher, and by his authority, I have recommended this translation of the works of the most illustrious Blessed Henry Suso <note>Henry Suso (c. 1295–1366) was a German Dominican mystic. His works were widely translated and adapted across Europe.</note> of the Holy Order of Preachers <note>original: "S. Ordinis Prædicatorum"; the Dominicans.</note>. This translation has been produced from ancient French and Latin codices <note>original: "Gallicanis & Latinis Codicibus"</note> by a humble and skillful hand, following the mind and spirit of the author. It adheres more truly to the context of the original language and dialect which was used somewhat widely and perhaps more crudely in the author’s own time among the Germans. While the author is commonly and canonically read in German, he was translated into Latin by the Venerable Laurentius Surius, a Carthusian. After most diligently examining this version, especially against the author's own copies from the Library of Cluny <note>The Abbey of Cluny in France held a massive collection of medieval manuscripts.</note> and other French sources reviewed by me, I have found nothing foreign to the Catholic doctrine of the Church or to good morals.

->Given at Cologne, June 1st, in the year 1661.<-

->Friar Nicolaus of Harburg, Lector of Sacred Theology and Preacher,<-
->Senior Prefect of the Order, General Apostolic Inquisitor,<-
->Primary.<-

---

# CENSORSHIP OF THE ORDINARY

Following the opinion and judgment of the Senior Inquisitor regarding the translation of these works—drawn from the German language into the French tongue <note>original: "ex Germanico idiomate in Gallicanâ linguâ"</note> by the Reverend Father Adrian von Walenburch, Doctor of Sacred Theology and Apostolic Prothonotary <note>A high-ranking official of the Papal Curia.</note>—I find nothing to prevent them from being printed, as they are useful and pious for the faithful and not contrary to good morals. Cologne, June 1st, 1661.

->Adrian von Walenburch, Archdeacon and Vicar<-
->General in Spiritual Matters for Cologne.<-
